title: Create and print a variable
starter_code: # Create a greeting variable and print it
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_greeting_variable():
    _old = sys.stdout
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = _old
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == 'Hello, Python!\n', f"Expected Hello, Python!, got {output!r}"

title: Swap two variables
instruction: Swap `x=5` and `y=10`, print both after swapping.
starter_code:
x = 5
y = 10
# Swap the values here
solution_code:
x = 5
y = 10
x, y = y, x
print(x)
print(y)
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_swapped_values():
    _old = sys.stdout
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = _old
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == '10\n5\n', f"Expected 10 then 5, got {output!r}"

title: Check variable types
instruction: Create int, float, str variables. Print their types.
starter_code: # Create three variables of different types
solution_code:
my_int = 7
my_float = 3.14
my_str = "hello"
print(type(my_int))
print(type(my_float))
print(type(my_str))
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_types():
    _old = sys.stdout
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = _old
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == "<class 'int'>\n<class 'float'>\n<class 'str'>\n", f"Expected int, float, str types, got {output!r}"
